itinerary.cal: Usually climbed in early summer, while snow still fills the slope up to the North Col and the moat below the east face is easier to cross; later in the season the moat can stop parties short of the rock. Bring an ice axe and crampons for the col.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: about 4 miles to the old Monte Cristo townsite (many parties bike it) and a rough trail to Glacier Basin, steep snow to the North Col, one short 5th-class pitch on the east face, then broken scrambling to the 7,136 ft summit. One rappel returns you to the base of the pitch. Expect 10 to 12 hours round trip.

days.title: Barlow Pass to the summit and back
days.objective: Climb from Glacier Basin to the North Col and up the east face to the summit, then return to Barlow Pass
days.note: Start early from Barlow Pass (about 2,300 ft) and walk or bike roughly 4 miles to the old townsite, then take the rocky trail past the waterfalls to Glacier Basin at about 4,500 ft. Climb the snow slope, or the spur beside it once it melts out, to the North Col; the steepest snow runs around 45 to 50 degrees and may need front-pointing. A short traverse from the col leads across the moat onto the east face, where one roped pitch graded about 5.6 (it feels stiffer) is followed by a ramp, a loose corner and heather to the top. Reverse the upper ground, rappel the pitch (a single 50 to 60 m rope reaches), traverse back to the col and down-climb facing in before glissading the lower snow.

schedule.label: Leave Barlow Pass
schedule.detail: About an hour to the townsite on foot or bike.

schedule.label: Glacier Basin
schedule.detail: Roughly an hour above the townsite; snow begins here early in the season.

schedule.label: North Col
schedule.detail: Steep, often hard snow just below the col.

schedule.label: East face pitch
schedule.detail: Cross the moat, climb one roped pitch, then scramble to the summit.

schedule.label: Summit, then rappel
schedule.detail: One rappel to the base of the pitch, then back across to the col.

schedule.label: Back at Barlow Pass
schedule.detail: About an hour from the col down to Glacier Basin, then the trail and the townsite road out.

itinerary.cal: Best from late June through mid-August. A wilderness permit is required and camps at Elk Lake and Glacier Meadows are limited, so reserve early. Bear canisters are required for all food and scented items, blue bags are required on the mountain, and there are no fires above Martin Creek. Early in the season steep snow lies on the trail between Elk Lake and Glacier Meadows, so an ice axe and crampons may be needed before the glacier.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days is the common minimum: a long, mostly flat walk up the Hoh valley to Elk Lake, a big summit day across the Blue Glacier, over the Snow Dome and up the West Peak's short rock summit block, then the walk out. Many parties add a day by camping higher at Glacier Meadows or on the Snow Dome.

days.title: Hoh trailhead to Elk Lake
days.objective: Walk the Hoh River Trail to a camp at Elk Lake
days.note: The first 13 miles follow the valley floor with little climbing; past the footbridge the trail starts to climb into the hanging valley that holds Elk Lake. Glacier Meadows, where the trail ends about 17.4 miles in, is the higher option and shortens the summit day. No camping is allowed between Glacier Meadows and the glacier.

days.title: Blue Glacier and the West Peak
days.objective: Cross the Blue Glacier and Snow Dome to the West Peak summit and return to camp
days.note: Above Glacier Meadows the climbers' path reaches the lateral moraine, where crampons go on for the lower glacier. Cross to the Snow Dome, climb loose scree and then snow to the upper ice, and rope up there for the crevassed ground below the summit. Skirt the bergschrund to reach the West Peak's summit block, where one short pitch of easy 5th-class rock leads to the top. Rappel the block and retrace the route to camp. From Glacier Meadows the summit is 4 to 6 miles one way.

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: An earlier start gives firmer snow.

schedule.label: Blue Glacier moraine
schedule.detail: Crampons on for the lower glacier.

schedule.label: Snow Dome and upper ice
schedule.detail: Rope up around 6,600 ft for the crevassed slopes.

schedule.label: West Peak summit
schedule.detail: About 8 hours from Elk Lake; one rappel off the block.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: About 14 hours round trip from Elk Lake.

days.title: Walk out the Hoh
days.objective: Return from Elk Lake to the Hoh trailhead
days.note: Descend out of the Elk Lake valley and follow the long, flat valley trail back to the trailhead.

itinerary.cal: Midsummer, once the south-side approach is mostly snow-free. The Gendarme pitches stay shaded and can be cold or icy. Carry plenty of water: the Cascadian Couloir descent is usually dry.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days from the Esmeralda (Ingalls) side: walk to a camp at Goat Pass, then climb the full ridge from its toe, descend the Cascadian Couloir and walk out over Longs Pass. Fast parties do it car to car in about 17 hours; parties who pitch out most of the ridge often bivy at the notch around 8,200 ft instead and take longer.

days.title: Esmeralda trailhead to Goat Pass
days.objective: Hike past Ingalls Lake and over Stuart Pass to a bivy at Goat Pass
days.note: Follow the Ingalls Way trail to Ingalls Lake, pass the lake on its west side and pick up the faint path to Stuart Pass. Cross talus below the West Ridge and, around 7,000 ft, drop into the north-side gully (not too early) before climbing out to Goat Pass at about 7,600 ft, which has many bivy sites.

schedule.detail: Keep to the west shore.

schedule.detail: Camp; snowmelt is the water source.

days.title: Direct North Ridge, Cascadian descent
days.objective: Climb the Direct North Ridge to the summit and descend the Cascadian Couloir to the car
days.note: Traverse east under the Stuart Glacier to the toe of the ridge. The first three pitches are the hardest of the lower ridge (a 5.8 slot and a sustained 5.9+ crack); above them mostly easy 5th class leads to the notch. The upper ridge brings a knife-edge and slabs to the Gendarme, climbed in two pitches (5.8 lieback, 5.9+ offwidth), then a 5.7 hand crack and broken ground to the 9,415 ft summit. Head east over the south ridge to find the top of the Cascadian Couloir, descend its long scree, and walk back over Longs Pass to the trailhead.

schedule.detail: About an hour to the base of the ridge.

schedule.label: Start climbing
schedule.detail: Three harder pitches, then simul-climbing on easier ground.

schedule.label: Gendarme

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: About 6 hours of climbing for a fast party.

schedule.label: Trailhead
schedule.detail: About 5.5 hours down the Cascadian and over Longs Pass.

itinerary.cal: Summer to early fall, once the west-side gullies at Washington Pass are melted out.
itinerary.totalNote: A single day from the Blue Lake trailhead: a short climbers' trail to the west face, five pitches of 5.8 to 5.9+ cracks (including an offwidth), then rappels down the west face and the walk back.

days.title: Blue Lake trailhead to the summit and back
days.objective: Climb the Northwest Corner to the summit of North Early Winter Spire and rappel the west face
days.note: Hike the Blue Lake Trail through its switchbacks for about two miles, then take the marked climbers' trail left to the foot of the Early Winter Spires and traverse north along the base of the north spire to the corner. Climb five pitches: a 5.8 corner with a short chimney, a 5.9 corner through trees, a 5.9 flake, the 5.9 offwidth that protects better than it looks, and a 4th-class traverse around the roof to the 7,760 ft top. Descend from the chains at the south end of the west face, making about six rappels on a single 70 m rope, including one free hang off a chockstone, then reverse the approach.

schedule.label: Blue Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: The climbers' trail branches left after about two miles.

schedule.detail: About 2.5 miles and 1,900 ft from the car.

schedule.label: Back at the base
schedule.detail: Climb and rappels, base to base, for a competent party.
